title: Managed Model Hosting Terms and Incident Escalation Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is an internal draft to capture proposed contract language and an operational playbook for 'Managed Model Hosting' engagements (includes Redwood-run private deployments, VPC-hosted, and on-prem managed installs). The intent is to give Sales/Legal/Infra a single reference that pairs legal obligations (data handling, liability, audit) with concrete operational steps and escalation timelines the SRE/PS teams can follow during incidents.

Scope / Audience:
- Applies to: commercial Managed Hosting agreements where Redwood retains operational responsibility for inference infrastructure and optional turnkey model management.
- Audience: Legal negotiators, Solutions Engineering, SRE, Professional Services, Customer Security.

High-level principles (for negotiation):
- Principle A: Customer data ownership and strict segregation. Redwood processes customer inputs/outputs only as described and returns or destroys customer data on termination.
- Principle B: Availability SLAs tailored by hosting mode (hosted API vs dedicated vs managed-on-prem).
- Principle C: Incident transparency + evidence obligations that balance customer assurance with Redwood security.
- Principle D: Limit liability proportional to committed fees and potential model IP exposure.

Key definitions (working):
- "Customer Data": all data supplied by customer for processing, including prompts, configuration, and custom fine-tuning artifacts.
- "Model Weights": model files (open or licensed) used to serve inference.
- "Managed Hosting": Redwood-operated stack (may be in Redwood cloud, customer VPC, or customer datacenter with Redwood access).
- "High-Severity Incident": event causing service unavailability > 15 minutes for an entire customer deployment or verified exfiltration of Customer Data.

Provider obligations (draft language snippets):
- Security Controls: Provider will maintain access controls, monthly vulnerability scans, quarterly penetration tests for managed-hosted components, and documented hardening for on-prem agents.
- Encryption: All Customer Data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys where requested (KMS/HSM integration). Transit TLS 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3).
- Logging and Isolation: Maintain tenant-level audit logs for control-plane and data-plane operations for at least 90 days (longer if requested as add-on). Logs shall not contain full prompt texts unless customer enables debug capture (explicit opt-in).

Data handling and sovereignty:
- Data residency options: region pinning for inference and storage; limited cross-border transfer only with written consent.
- Data minimization option: automatic prompt truncation & redaction rules to strip PII before persistent storage (configurable per customer).

Incident classification and escalation matrix (operational playbook):
- Detection: Telemetry sources: infra metrics, app error traces, customer error reports, external alerting (pagerduty).
- Triage steps (SRE):
  1) 0-5m: ack alert, create internal incident channel, initial severity, and paging.
  2) 5-30m: gather scope (impacted regions, models, customer tenants), apply runbook, attempt failover to fallback model/region.
  3) 30-120m: mitigation actions (rolling restart, scale-up, config rollback).
  4) 120m+: remediation plan and customer communications (see comms template).
- Escalation contact tiers:
  - Tier 1: Oncall SRE (pager).
  - Tier 2: Product-Infra lead (within 30m).
  - Tier 3: Engineering Director & Legal (within 2 hours for High-Severity incidents).
- Customer comms cadence (draft): Initial ack within 60 minutes for high-sev; status update every 60 minutes until service restored; post-incident report within 5 business days.

Evidence & audit playbook (for customer requests and audits):
- For audits: Redwood will provide an evidence package (redacted logs, attestation letters, config snapshots) within 10 business days for predefined standard scope.
- For deeper forensics (customer requests > reasonable scope): estimate and charge for professional services unless pre-negotiated in contract.
- Onsite or remote code review requests: handled as professional services engagement with NDA and scope.

Liability, remedies, and exclusions (negotiation positions):
- Liability cap: Provider prefers cap equal to 12 months of fees paid under the applicable order (common starting point).
- Carve-outs: willful misconduct, IP infringement, gross negligence excluded from cap.
- Remedies: service credits as primary remedy for SLA misses. Credits calculated as % of monthly fees proportionate to downtime beyond SLO thresholds.
- Data breach indemnity: provider to cover direct costs of remediation up to liability cap; carrier insurance check (Info: review cyber insurance limits pre-sign).

Availability SLAs (proposed tiers):
- Hosted API: 99.9% monthly uptime (standard), credits: 5% for <99.9, 10% for <99.5.
- Dedicated pool: 99.95% (higher ops commitment).
- Managed on-prem: SLA limited to agreed availability of the managed services only (not underlying customer DC hardware); suggestion: 99.5% with carveouts for customer infra failures.
- Note: latency SLOs are advisory metrics and not financialized in this draft.

Termination and data handback:
- On termination, Redwood will provide an export of Customer Data and configuration within 30 days in mutually-agreed formats.
- For managed-on-prem: plan handback steps (agent uninstallation, certificate revocation, KMS key access revocation).
- Secure deletion: Redwood to certify secure deletion of retained Customer Data within 60 days unless legal hold requested.

Model weights, derivative works, and IP handling:
- If Customer supplies fine-tuned model artifacts, Provider will not reuse those artifacts for other customers and will delete copies on termination unless otherwise agreed.
- Licensed model weights (third-party): clarify redistrib/use constraints and pass-through license obligations.

Negotiation & redlines (open items for Legal):
- Customer-managed keys: negotiate exact KMS support list and rotation responsibilities.
- Audit frequency and forensic evidence scope (quick wins: define a standard evidence package to avoid long tails).
- SLA credit calculation methodology and cap on credits (e.g., capped at a single month fee).
- Cyber insurance minimums: consider mandating minimums for certain enterprise customers.
- On-prem access windows: define scheduled maintenance and emergency access rights for Redwood staff.

Operational runbook examples (short):
- Example: KV cache corruption in dedicated pool:
  * Immediate: mark node read-only, initiate rolling restart, shift traffic to hot spares, notify customer with ETA.
  * Postmortem: cause analysis, mitigations, CPT, and data integrity verification steps.

Comms templates (snippets):
- Initial ack (60m): "We have acknowledged the incident and our team is working on containment. We will provide the next update by [time]."
- Post-incident summary: one-pager with timeline, impact, root cause, remediation steps, and compensations (if any).

Open operational questions (to resolve before finalizing contract template):
- Default retention period for pipeline logs (90 vs 180 days).
- Whether to allow debug capture (full prompts) in prod for more customers or limited to PS engagements.
- Escalation auto-notify to customer security contact vs only account team.

Change log (draft):
- 2025-11-08: initial outline (Asha).
- 2025-12-12: added incident matrix and evidence timelines (Liam).
- 2026-02-20: adjusted SLA tiers and clarified on-prem handback steps (Priya).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Legal to propose definitive liability cap language and carve-outs.
- Solutions Engineering to produce a short technical appendix (config names, agent ports, certs) for inclusion.
- SRE to validate the 60/120 minute operational timelines and provide any required tool integrations (pagerduty playbooks, runbooks).

Notes to negotiators (internal):
- Be conservative with liabilities on model-IP exposure; customers asking to host third-party licensed weights sometimes require additional indemnities.
- When a customer requests long retention or debug logs, surface to Pricing — this materially increases cost/ops burden.

-- end of draft --

[Unresolved redlines intentionally left inline above. This doc is for internal alignment; do not share externally without Legal review.]
